question: why does a 50,000-frame / 49-update R2 PPO run started from A0 move the 20-dev first-death mean from 1636.8 to 889.35 frames (-45.66%)?
declaration: R2 uses engine-truth reward and termination, so this is a training-time privileged diagnostic; nothing here is R1 or a capability claim.

headline.verdict: composite cause: an unanchored, metric-blind but large function drift

inputs.line_number_convention: touhou_rl/v420/rl.py line numbers refer to sha256 c0a5b8e426b8e46e4b1dd7d21f02c4be2fcf73548a8fa5e9b9fcf3814ea8ed16 (3832 lines); the file was edited by another agent mid-session (3821 -> 3832 lines, an episode-seed reporting fix in collect_rollout), which shifted later line numbers by 0-11 lines. Every reference also quotes the code fragment, so the fragment is authoritative if the numbers drift.

hypotheses.title: sampling temperature vs training temperature mismatch
hypotheses.one_line: rollout sampling and the update's log_prob recomputation use the same temperature field, so the ratio and the gradient are not computed in different spaces; the zero-update audit proves it numerically.

evidence.claim: there is exactly one temperature on the policy
rollout draws from log_softmax(logits / temperature)
the recorded log_prob comes from the same expression
the update recomputes it with the identical expression
the zero-update audit uses the same expression and finds max|ratio-1| = 9.537e-07
the temperature is read once from the frozen config
deployment is argmax of the RAW logits with no temperature

hypotheses.residual_finding: the temperature is not a ratio bug but it is a measurement bug: every logged health metric is computed on softmax(logits/8) while deployment is argmax(logits). See H4.

hypotheses.title: degenerate A0 plus 49 updates: how big is the damage per update?
hypotheses.one_line: Adam leaves a full lr-sized step on every minibatch, so 392 steps move the weights by 3.37e-03 - which is a 3.86-mean |dlogit| and a 61.7% argmax flip; 'max parameter change 2.40e-04' is not a small-update measurement.

evidence.claim: A0 at T=1 is degenerate
the same on the frozen teacher slots (my forward)
adam steps in the run
per update max |dW| divided by 8 minibatches equals the lr
measured cumulative max |dW| A0 -> R2
the functional change is not small
once the policy has moved, the within-update importance ratio is already far from 1 inside a single update
a max ratio deviation of 0.257 is 0.229 nat at T=8
the drift is concentrated in the shared feature extractor, not in the linear head
the critic shares the actor's trunk and back-propagates into it, so the value loss is a third gradient channel into the policy's features
evidence.where: rl.py:1270-1271 (one trunk feeds both heads), 1586-1589 (two lr groups), 1629-1632 (loss = policy + 0.5*value - 0.001*entropy, then loss.backward())

value.note: the value target is 99.8% a constant, so this channel carries no task signal either; it is consistent with the drift being concentrated in the feature layers, but it was not isolated in this round

hypotheses.correction: RL_PILOT2.md section 3.3 note 2 (line 243 at the time of writing) says the weights moved at most about 1.2e-2 from A0. That number is the no-sign-reversal bound 49 x 2.4031e-04 = 1.1775e-02; the measured cumulative maximum is 3.372e-03, i.e. the document overstates the weight drift by 3.5x. The correction does not weaken the diagnosis, because the functional drift is measured directly (61.7% argmax flips); the same note says 'argmax flips on many states' and this report replaces that with the measured 61.7%.

hypotheses.title: reward scale and advantage scale: is the advantage basically noise?
hypotheses.one_line: all 24 episodes end in game_over, so the -0.75 death term is a constant and var(return) == var(progress); the reward prices a 29.3% loss of first-death survival at 0.24% of return, while the critic's rmse is 63x the return sd and advantage whitening removes the amplitude anyway.

evidence.claim: return spread across the 24 episodes
the whole across-episode variance is the progress term
progress is 0.34% of the return and is bounded by 0.5
the reward barely ranks the metric the ruler measures

value.note: the death term is -0.75 in all 24 episodes, so the whole across-episode variance of the return is the variance of the progress term

evidence.claim: in-run degradation is almost free
the critic's error dwarfs the controlled quantity

value.note: normalise_advantages divides by the rollout advantage sd (rl.py 1582-1585), so whatever amplitude the advantage had is removed; the critic's own rmse is the scale of the thing being normalised

evidence.claim: advantages are whitened to unit variance, so amplitude cannot matter

hypotheses.title: are clip fraction and KL misread?
hypotheses.one_line: KL/entropy/clip are all computed on the T=8 tempered distribution, which understates the deployment (T=1) KL by the measured factor 11.6x; the deployed action distribution really did move (TV 0.42, idle 0.299 -> 0.511, 20/20 seeds), so this is a policy push and not an evaluation artefact.

evidence.claim: entropy, approx_kl and clip_fraction all come from the tempered probs
the same policy change measured in both spaces
the reported entropy is the tempered one, not the deployment one
evidence.where: pilot2.json statistics.entropy vs forward T1 entropies

evidence.claim: the deployed action mix moved, and the ruler is deterministic so it can only be the policy
the plan requires the KL to BC, and no such metric was ever recorded
evidence.where: README.md:237 ('record the KL to BC and the actual gradient magnitude'); pilot2.json contains only approx_kl

hypotheses.title: are the R0 and R2 evaluations comparable?
hypotheses.one_line: evaluator sha256, engine sha256, max-frames, obs-window, device, stage, difficulty and the 20 dev seeds are identical, and the gameplay-relevant engine data files are byte-identical; only the run-rewritten score.dat/modern-files.txt differ.

evidence.claim: evaluator sha256 matches the T04 declaration exactly
same engine on both sides
identical ruler arguments
the two data dirs differ only in files the engine rewrites
modern-files.txt differs only in the thread id
the ruler reproduces to 0.0 frames across campaigns
zero errors and zero invalid episodes on both sides
the record I compare against is the frozen R0 record

residual_risks.risk: score.dat is fully rewritten by every run (17785/17786 bytes differ) and is an opaque encrypted blob; it cannot be proven inert without the engine source
residual_risks.mitigation: both copies were already dirty before the campaign (score.dat.orig differs from both), and T04 reproduced two checkpoints with delta 0.0 across campaigns
residual_risks.status: not excluded by proof, excluded by measurement

residual_risks.mitigation: no episode timed out on either side (errors 0, invalid 0)

residual_risks.risk: the training env pulses SHOOT (rl.py:760-774) while the frozen evaluator never releases it (v410_student_eval.py:967) - a train/deploy mismatch shared by both arms
residual_risks.mitigation: 1 frame in 96; it is the mechanism the audit says is required to reach stage_clear, so it can explain 0 clears but not a -46% first-death drop

hypotheses.title: does the resume= wiring introduce a new bias?
hypotheses.one_line: reset() clears every per-episode counter and the accountant, GAE splits at every terminal, truncated transitions bootstrap V(s_T) and there were zero of them; the only new property of resume= is that an episode now spans several updates.

evidence.claim: reset clears frames/decisions/executed/buffer and re-seeds the accountant from the engine's own score
the episode is restarted before the 'rollout full' break, so the carry is never a dead episode
GAE never carries an advantage across a segment and bootstraps correctly
the truncation bootstrap is audited on a real truncated transition
the consequence that is real but not a defect
evidence.value: an episode is 1415-2950 frames = 1.4-2.9 rollouts, so the behaviour policy changes inside an episode; old_log_prob is recorded per transition (rl.py:1476) so the ratio stays correct, but the value targets mix states produced by older policies

agent.name: unanchored systematic function drift with no reward to resist it
gradient_channels_into_the_actor: value loss through the shared trunk (rl.py:1270-1271, 1629-1632)
entropy bonus with a fixed sign (rl.py:1641), which under Adam is a full-size step regardless of coef 0.001

enabling_condition_1.name: the reward cannot see the quantity the ruler measures

measurements.exchange_rate: 1% of first-death survival costs about 0.008% of return

enabling_condition_2.name: every health metric and the whole objective live in T=8 space

excluded_causes: resume= state leakage or TD misalignment (H6)

relative_contribution.not_available: no additive split of the -747.45 frames exists in this evidence; any percentage would be invented. What the evidence fixes is the ordering: the reward's blindness is why nothing resisted the drift, advantage whitening plus Adam is why the drift is large, and the T=8 metrics are why it was invisible. The agent of the observed change is measured directly: 61.7% argmax flips of which 58.2% of the logit variance is a single global action preference.

next_change.single_change: add one KL anchor to A0 computed on the UN-TEMPERED (T=1) logits: loss += beta * mean_t KL(softmax(z_A0) || softmax(z)), beta frozen at 1.0 before the run, with a fail-closed check that max_t KL_T1(A0 || pi_t) <= 0.05 nat over the 50,000 frames; beta may only be raised afterwards, never lowered.
why_this_one: it restores the KL-to-BC measurement README.md:237 already required and the run never recorded; the only KL in the payload is the within-update approx_kl
it acts in deployment space, where the collapse happened (T=1 KL 3.276 nat vs T=8 0.281 nat)
it leaves the reward and the learning rate untouched, so it is the one change that can separate 'the drift is the agent' from 'the reward is the agent'
it is scale-free: a plain learning-rate cut would also shrink any real signal, and Adam makes the lr a step-size not an amplitude control
not_recommended: lengthen the run or add steps
raise or lower the frame budget
add a survival reward term in the same revision (that is a second change and it destroys the discrimination)

P1_mechanism.claim: max_t KL_T1(A0 || pi_t) <= 0.05 nat over 50,000 frames

P2_function.claim: on the same 2x256 frozen slots: argmax flip rate <= 0.10 and max_a |mean_s dlogit(a)| <= 0.5

P3_behaviour.claim: the 20-dev diag_first_death mean lands in 1473-1800 frames (+/-10% of R0's 1636.8) and s1n in 2710-3313 (+/-10% of 3011.5)
P3_behaviour.band_rationale: the dev ruler is deterministic and paired on fixed seeds, so a departure from R0 is a policy difference, not measurement noise

P4_discrimination.claim: if P1 and P2 hold but the diag mean falls below 1473, the drift is exonerated and the next target is the reward/ruler misalignment quantified here (a 29.3% first-death loss cost 0.24% of return; corr(return, first_death) = 0.354 against corr(return, total frames) = 0.705)

falsifiable_prediction.what_the_change_cannot_do: it cannot produce a clear; 0/20 is expected on both arms at 50k

not_claimed: that the 61.7% flip rate measured on 2x256 D410-S1 seed-10/12 teacher slots equals the dev-level flip rate (the dev action mix is an on-policy measurement of a different state distribution)
any numeric split of the -747.45 frames into factors; the shares reported are shares of the measured logit variance and of the dev difference, not of the frame delta
that the KL anchor will improve capability; at 50k the most it can do is stop the drift
that score.dat is provably inert (the engine is a closed binary); it is empirically inert
that the train/eval SHOOT-pulse mismatch is quantified; it is identified in code only
that R0 was re-measured this round; R0 is the T04 frozen record, cross-checked byte-consistently across three files
any 1M-frame, 3-seed or R1 statement; R2 is a privileged diagnostic
that the run diverged in the PPO sense; KL and clip never blew up, this is silent drift
that the temperature is a ratio bug; H1 is excluded and the problem is the measurement space
blocking: a same-round A0 re-run on the 20 dev seeds was not allowed (it needs the engine); comparability is established by artefact identity, not by a live control
the score.dat inertness cannot be proven from the closed engine binary
no controlled ablation of the bias vs the reward was possible offline; that is what the P4 branch is for
